Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall retrieve the configured PSK from secure storage before initiating the DTLS 1.3 handshake.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the PSK is retrieved before transmission of the ClientHello message. Verify that handshake establishment is aborted if PSK retrieval fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall retrieve the configured PSK identity associated with the communication interface before initiating the DTLS handshake.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured PSK identity is available before the ClientHello message is transmitted. Verify that handshake establishment is rejected when no valid PSK identity exists.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall use the provisioned unique PSK associated with the configured SOW2–Vehicle ECU pairing during DTLS handshake key derivation.
The software shall ensure that the retrieved PSK remains within the secure cryptographic boundary throughout the handshake process.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the PSK is never exposed outside the configured secure cryptographic boundary.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall obtain random values required for DTLS cryptographic operations from a Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG) seeded by the hardware TRNG.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that random values are obtained from the approved random generation mechanism.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate a new DTLS Client Random value for every DTLS handshake before transmitting the ClientHello message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a Client Random value is generated before the ClientHello message is transmitted.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall not reuse a previously generated Client Random value for any subsequent DTLS handshake.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a unique Client Random value is generated for every handshake. Verify that previously generated Client Random values are not reused.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent reuse of random values across independent DTLS sessions.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that random values are unique for independent DTLS sessions. Verify that DTLS processing is terminated when random number generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate a new ephemeral ECDHE key pair before constructing the ClientHello message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a new ECDHE key pair is generated for every handshake.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate the ephemeral ECDHE key pair using the configured secp256r1 (P-256) named group.

The software shall ensure that the generated ephemeral ECDHE key pair is associated only with the current DTLS handshake and not reuse an ephemeral ECDHE private key or its corresponding public key for any subsequent DTLS handshake.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the corresponding public key is included in the DTLS key_share extension. Verify that each DTLS handshake uses a unique ephemeral ECDHE key pair. Verify that previously generated ephemeral ECDHE key pairs are never reused.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall ensure that the ephemeral ECDHE private key remains within the configured secure cryptographic boundary throughout the DTLS handshake.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ephemeral private key remains protected within the secure cryptographic boundary.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall operate as the DTLS 1.3 Client for the SOW2–Vehicle ECU secure communication interface.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that SOW2 initiates the DTLS handshake as the DTLS Client.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall include DTLS 1.3 as the supported protocol version in the supported_versions extension in the ClientHello message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ClientHello advertises DTLS 1.3. Verify that the handshake is terminated if DTLS 1.3 is not negotiated.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall include only supported DTLS 1.3 AEAD cipher suites in the ClientHello message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that only configured cipher suites are advertised.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall include TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 in the ClientHello message as a supported cipher suite for DTLS session establishment with the Vehicle ECU.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 is advertised

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall advertise the configured PSK-DHE key exchange mode with psk_dhe_ke in the ClientHello message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ClientHello advertises the configured PSK-DHE key exchange mode. Verify that unauthorized key exchange modes are not advertised. Verify that handshake establishment fails when the negotiated key exchange mode differs from the configured mode.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall encode the configured PSK identity using the configured identity format, encoding, and length before including it in the pre_shared_key extension of the ClientHello message.
The software shall include the generated ephemeral ECDHE public key in the DTLS key_share extension of the ClientHello message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the generated ECDHE public key is included in the key_share extension. Verify that the transmitted public key corresponds to the generated key pair. Verify that only the public key is transmitted.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if the generated ECDHE public key cannot be included in the key_share extension.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the handshake is terminated if the key_share extension cannot be generated.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall include the generated ClientRandom value in the ClientHello message
The software shall maintain the DTLS handshake transcript from the ClientHello until handshake completion by appending handshake messages in the order transmitted or successfully received.
The software shall maintain a retransmission buffer for transmitted DTLS handshake records until acknowledgement is received or retransmission is no longer required.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that transmitted handshake records are retained in the retransmission buffer until acknowledged or no longer required.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall start a retransmission timer after transmitting each DTLS handshake flight requiring acknowledgement.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the retransmission timer starts after transmission of a handshake flight requiring acknowledgement.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall retransmit unacknowledged DTLS handshake records when the retransmission timer expires.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that unacknowledged handshake records are retransmitted after retransmission timeout expiration.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall apply the configured retransmission timeout, timeout backoff policy, maximum retransmission attempts, and handshake timeout during retransmission processing.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured timeout, timeout backoff policy, retry limit, and handshake timeout are applied during retransmission processing.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if the configured handshake timeout expires or the maximum retransmission attempts are exceeded.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated when the configured retry limit or handshake timeout is exceeded.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall validate in ServerHello: the selected PSK identity received from the Vehicle ECU against the configured PSK identity. the selected cipher suite matches one of the configured supported cipher suites. the selected key exchange mode matches the configured PSK-DHE mode. the Vehicle ECU ECDHE public key before computing the shared secret.
The software shall verify that the cipher suite selected by the Vehicle ECU is one of the advertised and configured cipher suites.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that deprecated or unauthorized cipher suites are not advertised. Verify that the handshake is terminated when an unauthorized cipher suite is negotiated.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if the Vehicle ECU selects a cipher suite that was not advertised or is not supported.
The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if any mandatory ServerHello validation fails.
The software shall record a DTLS handshake failure in the security log when protocol version negotiation fails due to an unsupported or unauthorized protocol version.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify generation of a security event for protocol version negotiation failure like recording.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall compute the ECDHE shared secret using the locally generated ECDHE private key and the validated Vehicle ECU public key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify successful shared secret generation. Verify that shared secret generation fails when public key validation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall derive the DTLS handshake secrets using the configured PSK, the ECDHE shared secret, and the DTLS handshake transcript before processing encrypted handshake messages.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify successful handshake secret derivation. Verify that derivation fails when any required input is invalid. Verify that encrypted handshake messages are processed only after handshake traffic secrets are derived.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall derive the DTLS handshake write keys, write IVs, and sequence number encryption keys from the handshake traffic secrets.
The software shall receive the DTLS EncryptedExtensions message after successful derivation of the server handshake traffic keys.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the software processes the EncryptedExtensions message only after the server handshake traffic keys have been derived.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall decrypt the received EncryptedExtensions message using the server handshake traffic keys before processing its contents.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the software decrypts the EncryptedExtensions message using the server handshake traffic keys. Verify that the software validates the decrypted EncryptedExtensions message before continuing the DTLS handshake.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if the EncryptedExtensions message cannot be successfully decrypted or validated.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated if EncryptedExtensions decryption or validation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall receive and process the encrypted Finished message transmitted by the Vehicle ECU after successful completion of the preceding DTLS handshake messages.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the encrypted Finished message is processed only after the required handshake secrets have been successfully derived. Verify successful decryption of a valid Finished message. Verify rejection when decryption fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall decrypt the received Finished message using the derived server handshake traffic keys before performing verification.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated when Finished message decryption fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall ensure that the verification confirms that the Vehicle ECU successfully derived the same DTLS handshake secrets and processed the same handshake messages.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated when Finished message verification fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall discard the received Finished message when decryption or verification fails and prevent establishment of the DTLS secure session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the secure session is not established following Finished message verification failure.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall return only a generic handshake failure indication to the communication peer and shall not disclose whether the failure was caused by decryption, integrity verification, authentication failure, or handshake transcript validation.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that only a generic handshake failure indication is returned to the communication peer. Verify that detailed failure information is not disclosed through the communication interface.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall send the DTLS Finished message after successful verification of the Vehicle ECU Finished message.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS Finished message is sent only after successful verification of the Vehicle ECU Finished message.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall protect the DTLS Finished message using the client handshake traffic keys.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS Finished message is protected using the client handshake traffic keys.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if generation or transmission of the DTLS Finished message fails.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated if generation or transmission of the DTLS Finished message fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall wait for acknowledgement of the final DTLS handshake flight before considering the handshake successfully completed or shall retransmit the final handshake flight according to the configured retransmission procedure.
The software shall establish the DTLS secure session only after successful exchange and verification of Finished messages.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the secure session is established only after successful Finished message exchange. Verify that the secure session is not established when either Finished message verification fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall derive DTLS application traffic keys after successful completion of the DTLS handshake using the DTLS 1.3 HKDF-SHA256 key schedule.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that application traffic keys are derived only after successful handshake completion. Verify that application traffic keys are not derived following handshake failure.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall perform key derivation using the configured PSK, the ECDHE shared secret, and the DTLS handshake transcript.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that key derivation uses the configured PSK, ECDHE shared secret, and handshake transcript. Verify that DTLS processing is terminated when key derivation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall derive the DTLS application write keys, write IVs, and sequence number encryption keys from the application traffic secrets after successful Finished verification.
The software shall securely erase the ephemeral ECDHE private key after successful derivation of the DTLS session keys or upon termination of the DTLS handshake.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ephemeral private key is securely erased after session key derivation or handshake termination.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall enable protected SOME/IP communication and video streaming only after DTLS application traffic keys become available.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that protected communication is enabled only after application traffic keys are available. Verify that protected communication remains disabled when handshake completion fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall encapsulate application payloads within DTLS application records before applying DTLS record protection.
The software shall use the active DTLS application write state, including the application write key, write IV, epoch, and send sequence number, for transmission of protected application records.

The software shall encrypt all DTLS application records before transmission using the negotiated AES-GCM cipher suite using the active DTLS application traffic keys and ensure that plaintext application data is not transmitted after DTLS session establishment.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that AES-GCM encryption is applied to transmitted DTLS records. Verify that encryption uses the active application traffic keys.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall discard plaintext records received after establishment of the DTLS secure session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that plaintext records are rejected after secure session establishment.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall decrypt received DTLS protected records using the negotiated DTLS application traffic keys.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify successful decryption of valid protected DTLS records. Verify that unauthenticated application data is not delivered to upper software layers.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify the AEAD authentication tag before accepting the decrypted record.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify authentication tag verification for every received protected record. Verify rejection of records with invalid authentication tags.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall accept Vehicle ECU application records only when they belong to the active authenticated DTLS session.
The software shall generate a unique IV/nonce for each AES-GCM encryption operation performed during an active DTLS session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify generation of a unique IV/nonce for each protected DTLS record.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall ensure that IV/nonce values are not reused with the same cryptographic key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that IV/nonce values are not reused with the same application traffic key.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate record protection processing if a valid IV/nonce cannot be generated.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that record protection fails when IV/nonce generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent export of DTLS cryptographic key material outside the secure cryptographic boundary and prevent unauthorized software components from accessing DTLS cryptographic key material.
The software shall maintain an independent DTLS record sequence number for each active DTLS session and initialize the DTLS record sequence number when a new DTLS session is established.
The software shall assign a unique sequence number to every transmitted DTLS protected record.
The software shall prevent reuse of DTLS record sequence numbers within the same DTLS session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that sequence numbers are not reused within an active DTLS session.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall maintain an anti-replay receive window for each active DTLS session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that an independent anti-replay receive window is maintained for each active DTLS session.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify that the received DTLS record sequence number falls within the configured anti-replay receive window before accepting the record.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that received DTLS record sequence numbers are validated against the configured anti-replay receive window.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject duplicated DTLS records and records outside the configured anti-replay receive window.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that duplicated or out-of-window DTLS records are rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall update the anti-replay receive window after successful acceptance of a DTLS record.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the anti-replay receive window is updated after successful acceptance of a DTLS record.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall limit the DTLS application record payload size according to the configured DTLS record size and path MTU.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DTLS application record payload size complies with the configured maximum DTLS record size and path MTU.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent transmission of DTLS application records that exceed the configured runtime record size limits.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that transmission of DTLS application records exceeding the configured runtime record size limits is prevented.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate the freshness value as either a monotonic counter or a timestamp in outgoing SOME/IP responses and streaming video frames
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a freshness value is included in outgoing SOME/IP responses and streaming video frames when required. Verify that the configured freshness mechanism (counter or timestamp) is used. Verify that transmission is prevented when freshness generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall ensure that freshness values are not reused within an active DTLS session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that freshness values are not reused within an active DTLS session.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify the freshness value contained in received SOME/IP control messages and streaming video frames.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that freshness values are validated upon reception.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify that the received freshness value satisfies the configured ordering requirements and reject messages or streaming video frames whose freshness value is duplicated, expired, or outside the configured acceptance window.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify rejection of duplicated freshness values. Verify rejection of expired or out-of-window freshness values.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall discard rejected messages or streaming video frames before delivery to the upper software layer and continue processing subsequent valid messages after rejecting an invalid freshness value.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that rejected messages are not delivered to the application. Verify that valid subsequent messages continue to be processed.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall fragment outgoing DTLS handshake messages that exceed the configured DTLS handshake record size or path MTU.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DTLS handshake messages exceeding the configured record size or path MTU are fragmented before transmission.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall populate the DTLS handshake fragmentation fields, including fragment_offset and fragment_length, for each transmitted handshake fragment.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that fragment_offset and fragment_length are correctly populated for transmitted handshake fragments.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reassemble fragmented DTLS handshake messages before performing handshake message processing.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that fragmented handshake messages are successfully reassembled before handshake processing.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject incomplete, malformed, overlapping, or inconsistent handshake fragments.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that incomplete, malformed, overlapping, or inconsistent handshake fragments are rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake if handshake message reassembly cannot be successfully completed.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated when handshake message reassembly fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the DTLS handshake when negotiation of an unsupported DTLS feature is detected.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DTLS handshake is terminated when negotiation of an unsupported DTLS feature is detected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate a log entry immediately after detection of a security DTLS event.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DTLS security events are recorded. Verify that a log entry is generated immediately after event detection.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate a security event log entry for malformed records, invalid epoch, invalid sequence number, replay detection, AEAD authentication failure, decryption failure, freshness verification failure, and unauthorized command delivery attempts.
The software shall ensure that failure to record one security event does not prevent processing of subsequent security events.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that failure to record one security event does not prevent processing of subsequent security events.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent modification or deletion of recorded DTLS security logs by unauthorized entities.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that unauthorized modification of security logs is prevented. Verify that unauthorized deletion of security logs is prevented.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall ensure that DTLS security logs do not contain PSKs, DTLS session keys, handshake traffic keys, application traffic keys, ECDHE private keys, shared secrets, or other confidential cryptographic material.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that confidential cryptographic material is not stored in security logs.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall permit access to DTLS security logs only for authorized roles, authorized diagnostic sessions, or authorized service functions.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that unauthorized users cannot access protected log contents.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall store the trusted Root RSA public key used for SOW1 device authentication in protected non-volatile storage.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the Root RSA public key is stored in protected non-volatile storage.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent unauthorized modification, replacement, deletion, or disclosure of the stored Root RSA public key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that unauthorized modification or disclosure of the Root RSA public key is prevented.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject SOW1 device authentication if the Root RSA public key cannot be successfully loaded or validated.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that authentication is rejected if the Root RSA public key cannot be loaded or validated.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall request the SOW1 authentication data after system reset or before initiating the secured SOW1 video stream.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that authentication data is requested after reset or before secured video streaming.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall read the Device_n, KID, and Sig_device values from SOW1 through the I2C interface.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify successful reception of Device_n, KID, and Sig_device.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify that all required authentication fields are successfully received before initiating device authentication.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify rejection of incomplete authentication data.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the authentication procedure if the authentication data cannot be completely received.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that session establishment does not begin before authentication data acquisition completes.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify that the received KID corresponds to a supported cryptographic configuration.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify selection of the cryptographic algorithm associated with the received KID.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall select the RSA signature verification scheme and hash algorithm corresponding to the received KID.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify selection of the cryptographic algorithm associated with the received KID.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall perform RSA signature verification using the RSA verification scheme and hash algorithm selected for the received KID.
The software shall authenticate SOW1 by verifying Sig_device over Device_n and KID using the trusted Root RSA public key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify signature verification using the trusted Root RSA public key. Verify that trusted communication is not permitted before successful authentication.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject device authentication if Device_n, KID, Sig_device, or the selected cryptographic configuration is invalid, missing, malformed, unsupported, or if signature verification fails.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify rejection of malformed or unsupported authentication data. Verify rejection when signature verification fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate a fresh symmetric session key for each new SOW1–SOW2 secure session following successful completion of SOW1 device authentication.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a new session key is generated for every new secure session.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate the session key using a Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator (CSPRNG) seeded from the hardware TRNG.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the session key is generated using the approved entropy source.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent reuse of session keys across independent SOW1–SOW2 secure sessions.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that session keys are not reused across independent secure sessions.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate secure session establishment if session key generation cannot be completed successfully.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that secure session establishment is terminated when session key generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate row selection information for AES-CMAC calculation after successful session key generation
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that row selection information is associated with the active secure session.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate row selection information including the start row, row interval, and total number of selected rows.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify generation of start row, row interval, and total selected rows.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate two independent row selection information sets (Row_info_00 and Row_info_01) for the active secure session
The software shall maintain the generated row selection information unchanged throughout the active secure session unless a new secure session is established.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that row selection information remains unchanged during the active session.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate secure session establishment if row selection information cannot be successfully generated.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that session establishment is terminated when row selection generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall store the active session key only in protected memory allocated for the active secure session (DRAM).
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the session key is stored only within the authorized security processing context.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent unauthorized software components from accessing the generated session key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that only authorized software components can access the active session key.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent modification of the active session key after successful generation.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that unauthorized modification of the session key is prevented.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent storage of the session key in application logs, diagnostic responses, debug interfaces, memory dumps, or non-secure storage.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the session key is not exposed through logs, diagnostic responses, debug interfaces, trace outputs, memory dumps, or non-secure storage.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall perform encryption only after successful completion of SOW1 device authentication.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that encryption occurs only after successful device authentication.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall encrypt the generated session key and the associated row selection information before transmission to SOW1 using the authenticated SOW1 Device public key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the session key and row selection information are encrypted before transmission. Verify that encryption uses the authenticated SOW1 Device public key.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate secure session establishment if encryption of the session key or row selection information fails.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that plaintext session establishment information is never transmitted.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall transmit the encrypted session key and encrypted row selection information to SOW1 through the I2C interface after successful SOW1 authentication.
The software shall prevent transmission of unencrypted session establishment information over the I2C interface.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that session establishment is terminated when encryption fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall securely erase temporary copies of the generated session key after completion of the key-sharing procedure.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that temporary copies and working buffers containing the session key are securely erased after use.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent acceptance of authenticated video frames until successful completion of secure session establishment.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that authenticated video communication is blocked until secure session establishment completes.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall extract the embedded AES-CMAC authentication tag from the footer of each received SOW1 video frame.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify extraction of the embedded AES-CMAC tag from each received frame.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify that the authentication tag is present before initiating video frame authentication.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify rejection of frames with missing authentication tags.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject the received video frame if the authentication tag is missing or malformed.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify rejection of malformed authentication tags.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall prevent delivery of the received video frame for further processing until authentication tag extraction has completed successfully.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that frame processing does not continue before successful authentication tag extraction.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall select the active row selection information for AES-CMAC calculation according to the configured security selection state of the active secure session
The software shall recalculate the AES-CMAC authentication tag for each received SOW1 video frame using the active session key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify recalculation of the AES-CMAC for each received frame.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall calculate the AES-CMAC only over the configured image rows defined by the row selection information established for the active secure session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that only the configured image rows are included in the calculation.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate video authentication processing if AES-CMAC calculation cannot be completed successfully and prevent acceptance of the received video frames.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify rejection of the frame when AES-CMAC calculation fails. Verify rejection of the received video frames.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall compare the recalculated AES-CMAC authentication tag with the authentication tag extracted from the received video frame.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify comparison of calculated and received AES-CMAC tags.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall accept the received video frame only when the calculated and received AES-CMAC authentication tags match.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify acceptance of frames only when the tags match.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject and discard the received video frame if AES-CMAC verification fails.
The software shall generate a security event log entry when AES-CMAC verification of a received video frame fails.
The software shall continue processing subsequent received video frames following rejection of an individual video frame.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify continued processing of subsequent frames when permitted

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall verify the freshness of frame counter contained in each received SOW1 video frame.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that freshness information is verified when provided by SOW1.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall compare the received freshness information with the previously accepted freshness information associated with the active secure session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify detection of duplicated freshness values. Verify rejection of stale freshness values. Verify rejection of out-of-order video frames.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall reject duplicated, stale, or out-of-order video frames when freshness verification fails.
The software shall continue processing subsequent valid video frames after rejecting an invalid frame.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that subsequent valid frames continue to be processed.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall transmit protected SOW1 control commands only after successful completion of SOW1 device authentication.
The software shall include a monotonic counter in each protected SOW1 control command before generating the AES-CMAC authentication tag.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify inclusion of freshness information in protected control commands. Verify that freshness values are unique within the active secure session. Verify that transmission is prevented when freshness generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall ensure that freshness values are not reused within the active secure session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that freshness values are not reused.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall generate and append an AES-CMAC authentication tag for each transmitted protected SOW1 control command only when protected control command verification is supported by SOW1.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify generation of an AES-CMAC for each protected control command. Verify that the active session key is used. Verify that the authentication tag is appended before transmission. Verify that command transmission is prevented when CMAC generation fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall invalidate the active SOW1–SOW2 session key upon system reset, system restart, secure session termination, authentication failure, key sharing failure, or video authentication failure requiring session recovery.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify session key invalidation under all specified conditions. Verify secure erasure of invalidated session keys. Verify that invalidated keys cannot be reused.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall require establishment of a new SOW1–SOW2 secure session following session expiry, system reset, system restart, secure session termination, authentication failure, key sharing failure, or video authentication failure requiring session recovery.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that secure session re-establishment is required under all specified conditions.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall perform SOW1 device authentication before establishing the new secure session.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that SOW1 device authentication is repeated. Verify generation of a new session key and row selection information. Verify that trusted video frames are rejected until the new secure session becomes active.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The software shall terminate the secure session establishment procedure if completion is not achieved within the configured timeout period or retry limit.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify monitoring of secure session establishment duration. Verify termination when the configured timeout or retry limit is exceeded. Verify invalidation of partially established session information. Verify transition to the Inactive state. Verify initiation of recovery handling.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall keep the hardware debug interface, including JTAG, in the locked state by default when the ECU is in production mode.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that when the ECU is in production mode, the hardware debug interface, including JTAG, is locked by default after power-on/reset and cannot be used before successful secure debug unlock.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall permit hardware debug unlocking only through the approved UART-based secure debug unlock service.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that hardware debug unlocking is permitted only through the approved UART-based secure debug unlock service.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall reject any hardware debug unlock attempt received through any interface other than the configured dedicated UART service interface [X] [UART0, UART1, dedicated service UART, OEM-defined debug UART channel].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that any hardware debug unlock attempt received through an interface other than the configured dedicated UART service interface is rejected and does not enable the hardware debug interface.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall accept a debug unlock challenge request only when the request format is valid and the ECU lifecycle state permits debug unlock processing.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a debug unlock challenge request is accepted only when the request format is valid and the ECU lifecycle state permits debug unlock processing. Invalid format or unauthorized lifecycle state shall be rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall generate a fresh debug unlock challenge, KDF nonce, KDF salt, and Session_ID for each valid debug unlock transaction using the configured random source [X] [platform TRNG, TRNG-seeded CSPRNG].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that for each valid debug unlock transaction, the SW generates a fresh Challenge, KDF Nonce, KDF Salt, and Session_ID using the configured random source.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall ensure that the generated Challenge, Nonce, Salt, and Session_ID are unique per active debug unlock transaction and shall not reuse them for another transaction.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the generated Challenge, Nonce, Salt, and Session_ID are unique per active debug unlock transaction and are not reused across transactions.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall construct the debug unlock transaction context using the following fields: Challenge, ECU_ID, Nonce, Salt, Session_ID, and Validity_Period.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the debug unlock transaction context is constructed using the required fields: Challenge, ECU_ID, Nonce, Salt, Session_ID, and Validity_Period.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall bind the debug unlock transaction context to the target ECU identity format [X] [ECU serial number, ECU unique ID, VIN-bound ECU ID, OEM-defined ECU ID] and ECU identity encoding [X] [ASCII, UTF-8, binary].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the debug unlock transaction context is bound to the target ECU identity using the configured ECU identity format and encoding. A response using an incorrect ECU_ID shall be rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall configure the challenge validity period as [X] [30 seconds, 60 seconds, 120 seconds] and shall associate this validity period with the active debug unlock transaction context.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured challenge validity period is associated with the active debug unlock transaction and that responses received after expiry are rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall transmit to the debug tool only the debug unlock transaction context containing Challenge, ECU_ID, Nonce, Salt, Session_ID, and Validity_Period.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW transmits to the debug tool only the debug unlock transaction context containing Challenge, ECU_ID, Nonce, Salt, Session_ID, and Validity_Period, without exposing secret material.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall not transmit, process, or expect any algorithm identifier field during the secure debug unlock transaction because the secure debug mechanism uses a single fixed cryptographic profile.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that no algorithm identifier field is transmitted, processed, or expected during the secure debug unlock transaction. Any unexpected algorithm identifier shall not affect the fixed cryptographic profile.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall derive the DebugUnlockSessionKey from the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key using the configured KDF type [X] [CMAC-based KDF in counter mode, HKDF-SHA256, OEM-approved KDF].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DebugUnlockSessionKey is derived from the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key using only the configured KDF type.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall use the following KDF input fields for DebugUnlockSessionKey derivation: PSK, Nonce, Salt, ECU_ID, Session_ID, and debug unlock context [X] [SecureDebugUnlock, OEM-defined context string].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the KDF input fields include PSK, Nonce, Salt, ECU_ID, Session_ID, and the configured debug unlock context string.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall not use the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key directly as the AES-CMAC key for unlock response verification.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key is not used directly as the AES-CMAC key for unlock response verification.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall verify the debug unlock response using AES-CMAC with the derived DebugUnlockSessionKey.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that a valid unlock response generated using AES-CMAC with the derived DebugUnlockSessionKey is accepted, and an invalid AES-CMAC response is rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall construct the AES-CMAC protected input using the fixed field order: Challenge || ECU_ID || Session_ID || Nonce || Salt || Validity_Period.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the AES-CMAC protected input is constructed using the fixed field order: Challenge || ECU_ID || Session_ID || Nonce || Salt || Validity_Period.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall encode the debug unlock transaction context using a fixed canonical serialization format [X] [fixed-order binary concatenation, TLV format, OEM-defined canonical format] before AES-CMAC verification.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the debug unlock transaction context is encoded using the configured fixed canonical serialization format before AES-CMAC verification.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall encode multi-byte numeric fields in the debug unlock transaction context using byte order [X] [big-endian / network byte order, little-endian].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that all multi-byte numeric fields in the debug unlock transaction context are encoded using the configured byte order.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall maintain only one active debug unlock transaction at a time unless another approved policy is configured by response validation policy [X] [strict single-use challenge, single active challenge only, multiple pending challenges not allowed].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW maintains only one active debug unlock transaction at a time unless another approved response validation policy is configured.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall reject any unlock response that is expired, reused, malformed, invalid, unauthorized, or not associated with the active debug unlock transaction context.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that expired, reused, malformed, invalid, unauthorized, or non-associated unlock responses are rejected and do not enable the hardware debug interface.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall validate the received unlock response against the active transaction context, including Challenge, ECU_ID, Session_ID, Nonce, Salt, and Validity_Period.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the received unlock response is validated against the active transaction context, including Challenge, ECU_ID, Session_ID, Nonce, Salt, and Validity_Period.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall enable the hardware debug interface only after the debug unlock response has been successfully authenticated and verified inside the secure execution environment.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the hardware debug interface is enabled only after the debug unlock response has been successfully authenticated and verified inside the secure execution environment.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall prevent AES-CMAC key material, KDF intermediate values, derived debug session keys, and unlock verification material from being exposed through UART messages, logs, diagnostic responses, memory dumps, or non-secure storage.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that AES-CMAC key material, KDF intermediate values, derived debug session keys, and unlock verification material are not exposed through UART messages, logs, diagnostic responses, memory dumps, or non-secure storage.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall import or decrypt the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key only inside the protected execution environment using the ECU-specific OTP DEK.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key is imported or decrypted only inside the protected execution environment using the ECU-specific OTP DEK/KEK.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall store the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key only as part of an encrypted and authenticated ECU-specific key package in the configured SOW2 secure partition [X] [SPI secure partition, encrypted secure partition, secure storage partition].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the ECU-specific pre-shared debug authentication key is stored only as part of an encrypted and authenticated ECU-specific key package in the configured SOW2 secure partition.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall generate derived debug unlock session keys only for the active debug unlock attempt and shall not persistently store the derived session key.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that derived debug unlock session keys are generated only for the active debug unlock attempt and are not persistently stored.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall invalidate debug unlock temporary material, including KDF intermediate values and derived session keys, after unlock verification completes, fails, expires, or when the active transaction is terminated.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that debug unlock temporary material, including KDF intermediate values and derived session keys, is invalidated after verification completes, fails, expires, or when the active transaction is terminated.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall unlock the hardware debug interface only for a limited authorized debug session and shall automatically re-lock it after session timeout [X] [5 minutes, 10 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes] or upon completion of authorized debug activities.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that after successful unlock, the hardware debug interface remains unlocked only for the limited authorized debug session and is automatically re-locked after the configured timeout or completion of authorized debug activities.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall return the hardware debug interface to the locked state after every Power-On Reset.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the hardware debug interface returns to the locked state after every Power-On Reset.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall invalidate any active debug unlock session when the lifecycle state changes or when a security violation is detected.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that any active debug unlock session is invalidated when the lifecycle state changes or when a security violation is detected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall maintain a failed unlock attempt counter and shall apply the configured lockout policy after the defined number of failed attempts [X] [3 attempts, 5 attempts, 10 attempts].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW maintains a failed unlock attempt counter and applies the configured lockout policy after the defined number of failed attempts is reached.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall lock the UART-based debug unlock function for a configurable period [X] [30 seconds, 60 seconds, 5 minutes, until next POR] after the failed-attempt threshold is reached.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that after the failed-attempt threshold is reached, the UART-based debug unlock function is locked for the configured lockout period.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall return only minimum failure information over UART during failed unlock attempts and shall not disclose whether the failure was caused by challenge expiry, malformed data, invalid CMAC, wrong key, freshness failure, or authorization failure.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that during failed unlock attempts, the SW returns only minimum failure information over UART and does not disclose whether the failure was caused by expiry, malformed data, invalid CMAC, wrong key, freshness failure, or authorization failure.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall log debug unlock security events including challenge requests, successful unlocks, failed verifications, lockout events, and relock events.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that debug unlock security events are logged, including challenge requests, successful unlocks, failed verifications, lockout events, and relock events.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall include in debug unlock logs the configured timestamp source [X] [secure RTC, system monotonic counter, backend-provided timestamp], ECU identity, and transaction result.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that debug unlock logs include the configured timestamp source, ECU identity, and transaction result.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall restrict debug unlock log readout according to log access policy [X] [authorized debug session only, backend-authorized readout only, local diagnostic readout disabled].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that debug unlock log readout is restricted according to the configured log access policy and is not accessible through unauthorized interfaces or sessions.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall reject development or test debug authentication keys when the ECU is configured in production locked mode.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that development or test debug authentication keys are rejected when the ECU is configured in production locked mode.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support the selected secure debug key package provisioning configuration, including encrypted key package location and OTP DEK location, without exposing plaintext key values during runtime access.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the selected secure debug key package provisioning configuration is supported, including encrypted key package location and OTP DEK/KEK location, without exposing plaintext key values during runtime access.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall process only backend-generated unlock responses received through the debug tool over the approved UART debug unlock service and within the active challenge validity period.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW processes only backend-generated unlock responses received through the debug tool over the approved UART debug unlock service and within the active challenge validity period.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support secure boot chain-of-trust establishment from the read-only Root of Trust using public verification material provisioned in OTP/eFuse location [X] [SoC OTP/eFuse zone 7, other SoC-approved OTP/eFuse zone].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW establishes the secure boot chain of trust from the read-only Root of Trust using only the approved public verification material provisioned in the configured OTP/eFuse location.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall verify the authenticity and integrity of each boot image loaded from external SPI NOR flash before execution or transfer of control to the next boot stage.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that each boot image loaded from external SPI NOR flash is checked for authenticity and integrity before execution or before control is transferred to the next boot stage.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support the selected secure boot flow [X] [CV2xFS boot flow without OP-TEE, CV2xFS boot flow with OP-TEE if approved in future configuration].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW supports only the selected secure boot flow configured for the project, such as CV2xFS boot flow without OP-TEE or the approved future OP-TEE boot flow.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall verify the configured boot stages [X] [Safety BST, Safety BLD, Safety OS, A53 BLD, ATF, OS image] according to the approved boot chain sequence.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured boot stages are verified according to the approved boot chain sequence before each stage is executed.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall calculate the hash digest of each boot binary or firmware image using hash algorithm [X] [SHA-256].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW calculates the hash digest of each boot binary or firmware image using the configured hash algorithm, expected to be SHA-256.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall verify the RSA digital signature of each signed boot binary or firmware image using the public verification key provisioned in SoC OTP/eFuse zone [X] [zone 7, other SoC-approved OTP/eFuse zone].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW verifies the RSA digital signature of each signed boot binary or firmware image using the public verification key provisioned in the configured SoC OTP/eFuse zone.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support RSA signature verification according to RSA key length [X] [2048, 3072, 4096] bits and RSA signature scheme [X] [RSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW supports RSA signature verification using the configured RSA key length and RSA signature scheme. Unsupported key lengths or schemes shall be rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall confirm that the calculated image digest matches the authenticated digest before executing the image or transferring control to the next boot stage.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW confirms the calculated image digest matches the authenticated digest before execution. If the digest does not match, the image shall not be executed.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support the configured signature location/format [X] [image header, authenticated metadata block, end of binary] when locating and verifying boot image signatures.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW locates and verifies boot image signatures according to the configured signature location or format, such as image header, authenticated metadata block, or end of binary.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall fail the secure boot flow and prevent execution of the boot image if authenticity, integrity, boot metadata, hash digest verification, RSA signature verification, or anti-rollback verification fails.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the secure boot flow fails and the boot image is not executed if authenticity, integrity, boot metadata, hash digest verification, RSA signature verification, or anti-rollback verification fails.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall apply the configured secure boot failure action [X] [halt boot, reset, enter recovery mode, enter safe state] when secure boot verification fails.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured secure boot failure action is applied when secure boot verification fails, such as halt boot, reset, recovery mode, or safe state.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall apply the configured secure boot error reporting/logging policy [X] [no external detail, secure diagnostic event only, secure internal log only] when verification fails.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured secure boot error reporting/logging policy is applied when verification fails, and that no unauthorized external failure details are exposed.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall use authenticated boot metadata to support secure boot verification and anti-rollback protection.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that authenticated boot metadata is used to support secure boot verification and anti-rollback protection.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall process the configured authenticated metadata fields [X] [image identifier, image length, image version, boot stage ID, SHA-256 image digest, RSA signature information, non-volatile counter information, signature offset]. The SW shall support the configured metadata storage format [X] [image header, separate authenticated metadata block, appended footer].
The SW shall verify during firmware boot that the firmware version is not older than the minimum version authorized by the trusted monotonic counter.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that during firmware boot, the SW checks that the firmware version is not older than the minimum version authorized by the trusted monotonic counter.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall reject any boot image whose firmware version does not satisfy the configured anti-rollback check.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that any boot image whose firmware version does not satisfy the configured anti-rollback check is rejected and not executed.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support the configured anti-rollback counter width/location [X] [SoC OTP monotonic counter, OEM-defined non-volatile monotonic counter].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW supports the configured anti-rollback counter width and location, such as SoC OTP monotonic counter or OEM-defined non-volatile monotonic counter.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support the configured firmware version encoding [X] [integer version, security version number, image version field] for anti-rollback verification.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW supports the configured firmware version encoding for anti-rollback verification, such as integer version, security version number, or image version field.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall update the trusted anti-rollback counter only according to the configured counter update trigger [X] [after successful update, during production provisioning, OEM-authorized update package] and authorized updater [X] [OEM, Mekra production process, secure bootloader].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the trusted anti-rollback counter is updated only according to the configured counter update trigger and only by the authorized updater. Unauthorized counter updates shall be rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall restrict secure boot enable/disable controls and boot-device selection configuration to the allowed development lifecycle stage [X] [development, validation].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that secure boot enable/disable controls and boot-device selection configuration are restricted to the allowed development lifecycle stage only.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall enforce secure boot as permanently enabled when the ECU is in the mass-production lifecycle stage [X] [production locked, OEM-defined production lifecycle state].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that secure boot is permanently enabled when the ECU is in the configured mass-production lifecycle stage.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall prevent modification, bypass, or use of alternative development boot paths such as USB boot in shipped products according to disable mechanism [X] [OTP/eFuse configuration, secure boot lifecycle lock, SoC boot configuration lock].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that modification, bypass, or use of alternative development boot paths such as USB boot is prevented in shipped products according to the configured disable mechanism.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall use external SPI NOR flash as the selected production boot device when the ECU is in production mode.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that external SPI NOR flash is selected as the production boot device when the ECU is in production mode.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall allow boot-device selection to remain configurable only during the development lifecycle stage through the supported Power-On Configuration mechanism [X] [boot strap pins, SoC Power-On Configuration, OEM-defined development configuration].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that boot-device selection remains configurable only during the development lifecycle stage through the supported Power-On Configuration mechanism.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall support permanent production boot-device selection from the SoC OTP/eFuse field [X] [SoC boot-device selection field, OEM-defined OTP/eFuse field].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW supports permanent production boot-device selection from the configured SoC OTP/eFuse field.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall store security-sensitive assets requiring restricted access in protected storage type [X] [protected SECURE partition, encrypted secure partition, SoC protected storage, equivalently protected storage region].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that security-sensitive assets requiring restricted access are stored only in the configured protected storage type.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall enforce access to protected boot/security assets according to access control owner [X] [Secure ROM, secure bootloader, secure CPU, OEM-defined secure service].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that access to protected boot/security assets is enforced according to the configured access control owner, such as Secure ROM, secure bootloader, secure CPU, or OEM-defined secure service.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall use encryption/key source [X] [OTP-derived DEK, device-unique key, SoC secure storage key] where storage encryption is required for security-sensitive assets.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured encryption/key source is used where storage encryption is required for security-sensitive assets.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall protect security-sensitive data stored in external SPI NOR flash against unauthorized disclosure using protection mechanism [X] [encryption, secure partition protection, integrity protection with device binding].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that security-sensitive data stored in external SPI NOR flash is protected against unauthorized disclosure using the configured protection mechanism.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall not store private keys or other long-term secrets in plaintext in external SPI NOR flash.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that private keys or other long-term secrets are not stored in plaintext in external SPI NOR flash.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall bind security-relevant firmware or protected storage data to device-unique identity or device-unique cryptographic material [X] [device UID, OTP secret, OTP-derived DEK, device-unique cryptographic material].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that security-relevant firmware or protected storage data is bound to device-unique identity or device-unique cryptographic material.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall prevent operation of security-relevant firmware or protected data on unauthorized cloned hardware when SPI NOR flash contents are copied to another device.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that copying SPI NOR flash contents to another unauthorized device does not allow operation of security-relevant firmware or protected data.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall accept for execution only OEM-approved RSA-signed production firmware images that pass secure boot verification.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that only OEM-approved RSA-signed production firmware images that pass secure boot verification are accepted for execution. Unsigned or non-approved images shall be rejected.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall use only approved public verification material [X] [RSA public verification key, RSA public key hash, authenticated provisioning artifact] provisioned into SoC OTP/eFuse for production secure boot verification.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that only approved public verification material provisioned into SoC OTP/eFuse is used for production secure boot verification.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall not use, access, request, or depend on the OEM production RSA private signing key in the ECU runtime or production boot verification flow.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SW does not use, access, request, or depend on the OEM production RSA private signing key in ECU runtime or production boot verification flow.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall enable DRAM memory scrambling according to the configured production policy [X] [enabled in production, disabled only in development builds].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DRAM memory scrambling is enabled according to the configured production policy. In production mode, DRAM scrambling shall be enabled unless the approved policy explicitly allows disabling only for development builds.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall configure DRAM memory scrambling during the approved secure startup stage [X] [BST, secure bootstrap, early bootloader] before normal runtime execution.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DRAM memory scrambling is configured during the approved secure startup stage, such as BST, secure bootstrap, or early bootloader, before normal runtime execution starts.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall configure the SoC DRAM controller AES encrypt/decrypt engine such that all writes to external DRAM pass through the encryption path and all reads from external DRAM pass through the decryption path.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the SoC DRAM controller AES encrypt/decrypt engine is configured so that all writes to external DRAM pass through the encryption path and all reads from external DRAM pass through the decryption path.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall generate the DRAM memory scrambling key during secure boot using the configured entropy source [X] [SoC internal TRNG, Ambarella TRNG module/API].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DRAM memory scrambling key is generated during secure boot using the configured entropy source, such as SoC internal TRNG or Ambarella TRNG module/API.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall generate or configure the DRAM memory scrambling key with the configured AES key length [X] [SoC default AES key length, 128-bit, 256-bit].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the generated or configured DRAM memory scrambling key uses the configured AES key length, such as SoC default AES key length, 128-bit, or 256-bit.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall load the DRAM memory scrambling key into the configured write-only DRAM key register [X] [SoC write-only DRAM key register, Ambarella-approved write-only DRAM key register].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DRAM memory scrambling key is loaded only into the configured write-only DRAM key register.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall not provide any runtime software path to read back the DRAM memory scrambling key after it has been written to the write-only DRAM key register.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that no runtime software path exists to read back the DRAM memory scrambling key after it has been written to the write-only DRAM key register. Any attempted read-back shall fail or return no key material.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall configure the DRAM controller Address Translation Table for each configured DRAM client [X] [CPU, ISP, Video Codec, ETH-DMA, DSP, other DMA-capable clients].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the DRAM controller Address Translation Table is configured for each configured DRAM client, such as CPU, ISP, Video Codec, ETH-DMA, DSP, and other DMA-capable clients.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall assign each DRAM client only to its authorized physical memory range [X] [start address, end address, size].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that each DRAM client is assigned only to its authorized physical memory range according to the configured start address, end address, and size.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall configure DRAM access ranges during secure startup before enabling normal runtime execution and before enabling DMA-capable clients.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DRAM access ranges are configured during secure startup before normal runtime execution and before DMA-capable clients are enabled.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall define ATT access permissions for each DRAM client and memory range according to the configured permission set [X] [Read, Write, Read/Write, No Access].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that ATT access permissions are defined for each DRAM client and memory range according to the configured permission set: Read, Write, Read/Write, or No Access.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall prevent DMA-capable clients from accessing DRAM regions outside their configured ATT access ranges.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that DMA-capable clients are prevented from accessing DRAM regions outside their configured ATT access ranges. Unauthorized access attempts shall be blocked or handled according to the configured policy.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall apply the configured DMA/ATT violation handling policy [X] [block access, raise interrupt, report error signal, trigger controlled reset] when an unauthorized DRAM access attempt is detected.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that the configured DMA/ATT violation handling policy is applied when an unauthorized DRAM access attempt is detected, such as block access, raise interrupt, report error signal, or trigger controlled reset.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall isolate security-sensitive DRAM regions from non-authorized runtime software and unauthorized DRAM clients.
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that security-sensitive DRAM regions are isolated from non-authorized runtime software and unauthorized DRAM clients.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall include the configured security-sensitive DRAM regions in the protected memory map [X] [secure boot buffers, crypto working buffers, key-derivation temporary buffers, debug-authentication temporary buffers, security-relevant runtime buffers].
Verification criteria (from SRS): Verify that all configured security-sensitive DRAM regions are included in the protected memory map, including secure boot buffers, crypto working buffers, key-derivation temporary buffers, debug-authentication temporary buffers, and security-relevant runtime buffers.

Requirement (SOW2 SW, B-Sample SRS): The SW shall use the configured SoC-supported DRAM protection mechanisms [X] [ATT access control, secure boot-time memory map configuration, SoC hardware access restrictions] to enforce isolation of security-sensitive DRAM regions.
